chapter: Uniforms, funeral music and horn styles
title: A trumpet player people liked and disliked
summary: Rene criticises a player who played out of harmony, though audiences enjoyed his enthusiasm.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: That's funny, I heard a lot of people don't like him. What was wrong with this playing?

He had a funny way of playing playing that. It wasn't in harmony. And I couldn't say what kind of cause he was mad, because... But he had a kind of funny way of playing that. I ain't never heard of a kind of playing player like him. But I never did like it. Because then you would get some fellas come in and make some beautiful chords, you know. But he would be off, completely off of the band. And he'd play like that, play to his heart. And I don't see how a man there could be like that, but just that bad. That's right.
Some people like him and some people don't. That's funny.
Well, the people like him. He was a nice fella. And there's plenty of enthusiasm in his playing. Well, he was live with what he was doing. What he was doing was not. He'd be making a...
A guy like a roost singer. It all comes to me. Makes his horn go all kinds of funny ways. You see some people like that.
You get a kick out of that.
